subject: Post-demo: prompt collection & model fit next steps for ZenHealth

Subject: Post-demo: prompt collection & model fit next steps for ZenHealth

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Really appreciate the clarity on the two pilot workflows (clinical triage summaries and patient-facing Q&A). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) What we heard
- Clinical triage: short structured inputs (patient age, symptom codes, brief notes) -> concise summary + severity flag.
- Patient Q&A: free-form user questions about conditions, treatments; responses must avoid PHI leakage and incorporate provider-defined redaction rules.

2) Next steps (requested from you) — please: 
- Share ~50 representative real prompts for each workflow (can be de-identified) using the attached CSV template (zenhealth_prompt_template.csv). Prefer 30–50 examples per workflow; include edge cases and ill-formed user inputs.
- Provide your redaction rules doc or a brief bullet list of what counts as PHI for ZenHealth (we'll mirror that in evals).
- Call out any forbidden behaviors (e.g., diagnosis statements vs. educational language).

3) What we'll do on our side
- Run a lightweight model-fit eval on 3 candidate models with your sample prompts: one small/high-throughput (MPT-7B), one medium/balanced (Llama-2-13B), one high-capacity (Llama-2-70B or equivalent), plus a quantized variant for throughput checks.
- Share a short benchmark report (latency, 95th pct latency, token cost estimate, and a small quality rubric) — draft attached (redwood_eval_benchmark_report.pdf).
- Highlight any quality regression risks we see and recommended prompt redaction/normalization.

4) Logistics and timeline
- If you can drop prompts + redaction guidance by EOD Monday (2026-06-15), we'll return initial evals by end of week (2026-06-19).
- If helpful, happy to put together a 30-min workshop with your clinical SME to walk through edge cases.

Attachments: zenhealth_prompt_template.csv (template), redwood_eval_benchmark_report.pdf (example).

Thanks — small asks = big impact on eval quality.

—Markus Klein

Thanks Markus — great summary. Attaching an initial batch inline below and a short redaction note. Tom, feel free to add.

Short redaction rules (high level):
- Remove direct identifiers: names, addresses, SSNs, MRNs. Replace with tokens (PATIENT_NAME_1, MRN_XXXXX).
- Dates: keep relative ages ("3 months ago") rather than exact DOBs.
- Free-text clinician notes: patient identifiers scrubbed; keep symptom phrases intact.
- Do not include raw device IDs or secure links.

Sample prompts (10 mixed examples, will upload CSV by Monday):
1) "My chest is tight and I've been coughing for 3 days — what should I do?"
2) "PATIENT_NAME_1 had a fever of 102F last night and is showing rash on torso."
3) "My meds are lisinopril and metformin, can I take ibuprofen with them?"
4) "I lost my appointment confirmation link, can you resend?"
5) "PATIENT_NAME_2 reports severe headache after skiing — emergency?"
6) "What does the lab result 'eGFR 48' mean for kidney function?"
7) "Is it safe to breastfeed on this medication?"
8) "Patient has an allergy to penicillin, prescribe alternatives."
9) "How long should concussion symptoms last after a fall?"
10) "I can't read my lab PDF (link removed), can you summarize the numbers?"

Edge cases to flag: chained prompts (user follows up with new symptom), prompts with partial PHI tokens, and many short one-word inputs ("nausea").

We'll upload a CSV and a short redaction checklist by Monday EOD. Thanks for running the evals — please prioritize the triage summary workflow first.

—Aisha
Head of Clinical Products, ZenHealth
aisha.ndiaye@zenhealth.ai

Markus / Camila — forwarding Aisha's sample prompts. A few internal notes / asks for the eval team before we kick off: 

- Priority: triage summary workflow (short structured input). Run both quality and latency slices: 1) median latency under 250ms target for small payloads, 2) 95th percentile under 800ms for our Dedicated baseline.
- Candidate models to benchmark (provisional): MPT-7B-instruct, Llama-2-13B-chat, Llama-2-70B-chat (quantized q4 for throughput). Please include an embeddings-run for semantic search fallback using OpenAI-compat embeddings if we need reranking.
- Evaluation rubrics: factuality for clinical facts (3-pt scale), redaction compliance (pass/fail), helpfulness/conciseness. Use the CSV schema in the attachment for marking.
- Compliance note: Aisha's team will only upload de-identified tokens; still treat as protected in our environment. Confirm that Dedicated sandbox will mask logs and that retention defaults to 30 days for these pilot evals. If retention policy differs, flag it immediately so Markus can escalate.

Camila — can you schedule a quick 30-min call with the evaluation engineers (Neha, Camila, Viktor) and ZenHealth's clinical SME for Monday 6/15? Markus — please propose 30-min blocks after 10am PT.

Thanks — Neha
